requirement: The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas` skill must tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_starts_a_new_project_with_the_requirements_skill]` covers it:
- It uses `step("habeas", 1)` to read the numbered routing step of the bundled `habeas` skill's Workflow section.
- `workflow_steps` panics if the skill has no Workflow section or the step is missing.
- It asserts with `assert_text` that the step contains the sentence "A new project with little code starts with habeas-requirements, not habeas-bootstrap-requirements, even though most of its code has no references". `assert_text` uses `contains` and fails with a message if the phrase is absent.
- That phrase carries every clause of the requirement: the new-project condition, the choice of `habeas-requirements`, the exclusion of `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, and the "most code has no references" caveat.
- It also asserts the contrasting bootstrap routing row, "Adopting Habeas in an existing codebase, or most of the code has no references | habeas-bootstrap-requirements". That check shows the new-project guidance sits beside the bootstrap guidance it is distinguished from.

The test reads the real bundled skill text, so removing or changing the guidance would fail it. The requirement has no other modes or boundary cases. I found no gaps.
